title: Gumroad pricing
finding: Direct sales 10% + US$0.50; Discover sales 30%; merchant-of-record model. Processor charges and refunds require current help-page review.

title: Gumroad fees help
finding: Direct sale platform fee is 10% + US$0.50; processor fees can be additional. Discover 30% includes processing. Do not model every direct sale at only 10%.

title: Lemon Squeezy pricing
finding: Base digital-product processing 5% + US$0.50, no monthly processing subscription; merchant of record.

title: Lemon Squeezy fee details
finding: Adds 1.5% for non-US transactions, 1.5% PayPal, 0.5% subscriptions; fees on order total including tax. Non-US bank payout fee 1%. Other marketing fees can apply.

title: Lemon Squeezy supported countries
finding: Canada appears in supported bank-payout countries. Business approval and identity verification remain necessary; some customer countries are excluded.

title: Lemon Squeezy prohibited products
finding: Product-category approval is required; consult prohibited-product rules before selecting it for a service, marketplace or AI product.

title: itch.io payment documentation
finding: Open revenue sharing; example uses default 10% plus generally 2.9% + US$0.30 processor charges. Direct and collected-payout modes differ, as do tax and payout obligations.

title: Fab publisher programme
finding: Publishers receive 88% revenue share; supports multiple engines and digital asset types. Acceptance, tax interview and payout onboarding required.

title: Unity publishing
finding: No publishing fee; publishers retain 70%; minimum asset price US$4.99. Submission review and tax/payout profile required.

title: Godot Asset Store submission
finding: Paid assets cannot yet be uploaded. Functional assets, correct licences and AI disclosure required.

title: Godot store roadmap
finding: Buy/sell support remains a future feature; roadmap text may lag release status, so do not assume future paid checkout availability.

title: Godot engine licence
finding: Commercial games allowed; MIT notice obligations apply. Engine permission does not licence third-party game characters, art, music or assets.

title: Current paid game asset listings
finding: Approximately 59,951 paid listings displayed at research time. Evidence of substantial supply, not buyer counts or seller profitability.

title: Modular low-poly city pack
finding: US$19 list price and US$9.50 sale price observed. A live offer demonstrates asking price, not sales or profit.

title: Kenney asset catalogue
finding: Broad free asset catalogue including 2D, 3D, UI, audio and textures; strong substitute for generic packs.

title: Godot save system competitors
finding: Many paid and free save-system listings; observed paid examples around US$3–15. Generic save plugins face substantial price pressure.

title: Greenlight web export toolkit
finding: Free MIT toolkit checks several Godot web-export issues. Listing updated 10 October 2026 and marked unstable. Strong substitute; no paid-demand proof.

title: Godot command line documentation
finding: Headless command-line exports supported; installed editor/export templates and matching export preset required.

title: Godot export troubleshooting
finding: PCK paths are case-sensitive; missing resources and case mismatch can break export. Older documentation establishes problem, not current prevalence.

title: Khronos glTF validator
finding: Existing browser and CLI validators produce structured asset reports; reuse only after reviewing current licence, rather than rebuilding basic validation.

title: Weblate quality checks
finding: Existing localization checks cover placeholders, plurals, markup and format errors. Strong free/self-hosted substitute; linguistic correctness still needs judgment.

title: Weblate pricing
finding: Hosted localization products have paid plans. Header starts at EUR39/month; specific monthly/annual and string-count prices must be checked in calculator.

title: CSVbox pricing
finding: CSV validation/import product with sandbox and paid plans; Startup displayed US$16/month billed yearly. Many capabilities already commoditized.

title: Dromo pricing
finding: Professional advertised US$599/month including 250 production imports then US$3/import. Enterprise features and security claims are vendor statements.

title: PDFMonkey pricing
finding: September 2026 page: free 20 documents/month; Starter EUR5/month for 300, Pro EUR15/month for 3,000. Generic rendering is inexpensive.

title: Distill pricing
finding: Website-change monitoring free tier and US$15/35/80+ monthly plans. Offer has strong free competition; target monitoring requires permission/terms review.

title: ScreenshotOne founder milestone
finding: 10 April 2025 founder report: US$200,000 ARR and 400+ paying customers after nearly three years. Unaudited revenue, not net profit or typical results.

title: ScreenshotOne company information
finding: Company describes itself as bootstrapped and profitable. No audited current income statement inspected.

title: Remote OK employer checkout
finding: Job posting starts at US$299 for 30 days with dynamic pricing and optional paid additions. Renewal and refund terms matter; audience claims are vendor claims.

title: GDQuest course offers
finding: Specialized Godot learning products have paid offers. Search crawl was older, so exact prices are not treated as live validated launch anchors.

title: GDQuest lifetime-bundle change
finding: 2023 explanation says continuing development does not fit unlimited lifetime-future-content pricing. Historical lesson, not current revenue evidence.

title: Notion template selling
finding: 8% + US$0.40; non-US payout FX fee 1%; Canada supported; approval/waitlist can take months; payout holds and minimum apply.

title: Etsy fees
finding: US$0.20 listing charge and 6.5% transaction fee; extra processing, regulatory, FX and Offsite Ads fees can apply. Setup fee may be shown on onboarding.

title: Etsy Payments
finding: Canada domestic/US orders 3% + CAD0.25; other international orders 4% + CAD0.25, exclusive of applicable tax.

title: Etsy creativity standards
finding: Seller-prompted AI creations have conditions; original design responsibility remains. AI prompt bundles do not qualify. Check current disclosure requirements.

title: Adobe Stock generative AI rules
finding: June 2026 guidance permits qualifying, labelled AI images/vectors/videos; rights and technical quality required; excessive similar submissions are spam.

title: Adobe Stock royalties
finding: 33% content-revenue royalty described for qualifying photos/illustrations/vectors, with pooled allocation for Pro Edition. Individual download values vary.

title: KDP ebook royalties
finding: 35% or qualifying 70% royalty; delivery costs, customer territories, price rules and refunds matter. Not a universal 70% margin.

title: KDP content policy
finding: AI-generated text/images/translations require disclosure to KDP; AI assistance treated differently; rights and customer-quality obligations apply.

title: TPT seller fees
finding: Basic: US$29 one-time, 55% payout and US$0.30/resource. New Exclusive: US$59.95/year, 80% through 2026 then 77.5% from 2027; exclusivity applies.

title: TPT exclusivity
finding: Exclusive sellers must sell digital educational resources through TPT; conflicts with a multi-checkout portfolio. Existing Premium programme changed.

title: Udemy course revenue share
finding: 97% on qualifying instructor-referred course transactions versus 37% otherwise; other deductions and refunds affect earnings.

title: Udemy subscription pool
finding: 2026 subscription instructor pool is 15% of eligible subscription revenue and allocated by learner engagement, not 15% of an individual's course price.

title: Printful costs
finding: Free account option; merchant pays product/printing/shipping/tax on orders. Customer storefront receipts and fulfilment billing have separate cash timing.

title: Printful returns
finding: Buyer remorse/wrong size not covered by standard fulfilment returns. Seller's consumer-law obligations remain; defect/loss claim deadlines apply.

title: Amazon Canada commission rates
finding: Category rates range from zero to 10%; computers/consoles 1% and many categories 3–6%. Refunds and attribution conditions reduce payable commissions.

title: Amazon Associates policies
finding: Link, content, attribution, promotion and payout rules apply; no fake reviews, self-dealing or unauthorized product-data reuse.

title: Shopify app distribution
finding: Eligible reduced programme: 0% on first US$1m and 15% afterward; registration/eligibility and billing requirements apply. Protected customer data adds obligations.

title: Chrome developer account
finding: One-time registration fee and developer agreement required. Amount should be verified at onboarding; external billing and privacy implementation needed.

title: Figma paid resources
finding: 15% fee; Canada supported. New paid-file creator approval is paused; do not assume paid-file access. Plugins/widgets have separate rules.

title: Superhive creator pricing
finding: Free plan: 70% commission less US$0.49 item fee and 5.5% merchant fee; paid plans raise commission but add recurring fees. Review actual calculator before use.

title: Creative Market earnings
finding: Default creator share 50%; rates vary by shop/product. Discounts can affect earnings.

title: Canva Creators
finding: Application/portfolio required; element creator application paused. Qualifying creators earn royalties, not a guaranteed per-template return. Heavy AI-generated submissions restricted.

title: Blender extension platform
finding: Official extension platform offers GPL-compliant software. Monetization and redistribution rights require licence-aware packaging.

title: WordPress plugin developer rules
finding: Repository restrictions on trialware/licence gates apply. A separately distributed paid add-on or genuine service must comply with detailed rules.

title: VS Code extension publishing
finding: Marketplace publication workflow and security requirements documented. Global PAT retirement announced for 1 December 2026; use supported secure publishing.

title: Monotype foundry royalties
finding: Foundry guidance advertises 50% on MyFonts and 25% on other covered channels. Actual agreement and eligible rights govern.

title: Canada open licence
finding: Commercial reuse of covered information allowed with attribution; excludes personal information, third-party rights and official marks; no endorsement.

title: CanadaBuys dataset
finding: Tender-notice CSV feeds available under Open Government Licence. Data freshness and individual attachment rights still need checks.

title: Statistics Canada developer access
finding: Web Data Service, daily deltas and CSV tables available; preserve units, vintages and revision metadata.

title: Statistics Canada licence FAQ
finding: Covered open information can be commercially redistributed; not all restricted microdata or separately licensed products are included.

title: MERX pricing
finding: Canadian national tender subscription advertised CAD80/month annual billing or CAD160/month monthly billing. Broader coverage than a federal-feed-only product.

title: Cloudflare Workers pricing
finding: Workers paid base US$5/month; static requests free; requests, CPU, storage and other products have quotas/overages. Free plans unsuitable for unbounded guarantees.

title: Stripe Canada pricing
finding: Domestic cards 2.9% + CAD0.30; international +0.8%, FX +2% when applicable. Billing/tax/disputes are additional products or fees.

title: GitHub Pages limits
finding: GitHub Pages may not be used as free hosting primarily for ecommerce/commercial SaaS. Use appropriate commercial hosting.

title: n8n licensing guidance
finding: Community licence permits bounded internal uses; hosting n8n as a service/white-labelling requires commercial licensing. Verify use-specific terms.

title: Google spam policy
finding: Scaled content and doorway abuse can remove search visibility. AI-generated volume is not a durable distribution strategy.

title: CASL guidance
finding: Commercial electronic messages generally need consent, identification and unsubscribe. Asking for consent by unsolicited commercial email is itself covered.

title: CASL FAQ
finding: Express/implied consent conditions vary; public address is not blanket permission. Keep evidence and honour opt-outs.

title: CRA GST HST registration
finding: CAD30,000 small-supplier threshold concerns worldwide taxable supplies across businesses and associates, with single-quarter and rolling-quarter timing rules.

title: CRA business reporting
finding: Sole proprietors generally report business income and expenses on T2125; income tax differs from sales tax.

title: CRA record retention
finding: Business records generally retained at least six years from end of relevant tax year; track gross income, fees, expenses and supporting documents.

title: OPC privacy guide
finding: Accountability, meaningful consent, safeguards, limited collection/retention and breach obligations matter. Provincial and international rules may also apply.

title: Competition Bureau disclosures
finding: Material connections in promotion require clear disclosure; avoid unsubstantiated performance claims and disguised advertisements.

title: YouTube originality policy clarification
finding: Mass-produced/repetitive inauthentic content ineligible for monetization; AI use alone is not the sole test.

title: Steam Direct fee
finding: US$100 or equivalent fee per app; recoupment conditions apply. This does not establish a standard distribution revenue split.

title: CrazyGames developer FAQ
finding: Advertising revenue share and optional in-game purchases; publication on other platforms generally compatible. Review current contract and approval before budgeting.

title: Godot shader licence examples
finding: Shader code licences can be CC0, MIT or GPL; preview art/video is not automatically covered. Many free substitutes.

title: UI audio marketplace
finding: Paid UI sound packs at diverse prices, including US$1–15 examples. Listings show competition, not verified earnings.

title: Printables clubs
finding: Creator memberships and exclusive model catalogues exist; exact current seller fees and Canada payout eligibility not verified in this review.

title: Papa Parse
finding: Browser-local CSV parsing, streaming, worker support and structured parsing errors; pin and review the actual dependency version before shipping.

title: Ajv JSON schema validator
finding: Reusable JSON Schema validation library; review bundled version, licence and security before redistribution.

title: FormatJS
finding: ICU message-format tooling can support parsing; integrate only the needed package and preserve required notices.

title: Lemon Squeezy webhooks
finding: Order/subscription/refund events supported; verify signatures, persist events and process idempotently. Provider retries are finite, so reconcile separately.

title: Lemon Squeezy licensing
finding: Managed licence keys are available; do not put private API keys in client apps or make bought offline files unusable during a billing outage.

title: GitHub Actions billing
finding: CI free allowances depend on plan/repository/runner type. Configure spending limits and avoid assuming every private-repo build is free.

title: Playwright
finding: Browser testing framework supports Chromium, Firefox and WebKit; useful for checkout and UI regression tests.

title: Lemon Squeezy payout timing and minimum
finding: Payout timing, holds and US$50 threshold inform cash-timing assumptions. Actual account approval and first settlement may differ.

title: Lemon Squeezy refunds and chargebacks
finding: Refund/dispute handling and a US$15 chargeback fee inform the conservative model. Check applicable current transaction reversal treatment before launch.
